name: Primary Acquired Pure Red Cell Aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Acquired Pure Red Cell Aplasia

criteria.description: Severe normocytic normochromic anemia with reticulocytopenia
Bone marrow biopsy showing marked erythroid hypoplasia or aplasia with normal granulopoiesis and megakaryopoiesis
Exclusion of secondary causes such as thymoma, lymphoproliferative disorders, infections, or drug-induced PRCA
Absence of hemolysis or other causes of anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe anemia with reticulocytopenia, bone marrow erythroid aplasia, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary etiologies and confirmation by bone marrow biopsy.

searchTerms: severe anemia with normal cell size
low red blood cells normal shape
pale skin from low red blood cells
skin looks lighter due to anemia
fatigue related to low red blood cells
fast heart rate due to anemia

occasional.symptomName: Mild jaundice due to ineffective erythropoiesis
searchTerms: jaundice due to poor red cell production
head pain from low blood count

rare.notes: Rarely present in primary acquired cases but important to exclude secondary causes

searchTerms: brain or nerve problems due to hypoxia

laboratory: Severe anemia with low reticulocyte count
Normal white blood cell and platelet counts
Absence of hemolysis markers (normal LDH, bilirubin)
imaging: Chest imaging to exclude thymoma or mediastinal masses
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified in primary acquired PRCA
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing selective erythroid aplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Bone marrow hypocellularity involving all hematopoietic lineages
Presence of underlying conditions such as thymoma, infections, or drug exposure
Resolution of anemia after treatment of underlying cause
Dysplastic changes in bone marrow cells

redFlags: Rapidly worsening anemia with hemodynamic instability
Presence of pancytopenia suggesting aplastic anemia
Evidence of thymoma or other malignancy on imaging
